items.title: The Amazon generates much of its own rainfall
items.claim: How much of South American rainfall depends on Amazon transpiration?

options.text: None — rainfall comes entirely from the Atlantic

Amazon trees transpire huge volumes of water vapour, recycling moisture 5-6 times across the basin and generating 'flying rivers' that supply rainfall to southeast South America — including Brazil's agricultural heartland

items.reveal:
A mature Amazon tree can transpire 200-1,000 litres per day. The 'flying river' concept, popularised through INPE (Brazilian space agency) research and Antonio Nobre's work, describes the moisture flux from the basin southward — equivalent to or exceeding the Amazon River's surface discharge.

Deforestation reduces transpiration. Gatti et al. (Nature 2021) showed that the southern and eastern Amazon are already becoming net carbon sources. A tipping point at around 20-25% deforestation could shift large parts of the forest to savannah — with major consequences for Brazilian rainfall and agriculture.

Current deforestation is around 17-20% of the original Amazon area.
items.why: Forests are climate machines. Amazon loss would change rainfall patterns far beyond the basin — and threaten the agricultural economy that has driven much of the deforestation in the first place.

items.title: Meanders migrate downstream over time
items.claim: What happens to meanders over years to decades?

options.text: They are fixed features that maintain their shape
Erosion on the outer bank and deposition on the inner bank cause meanders to migrate downstream and laterally, eventually being cut off as oxbow lakes
Meanders only form in glacial rivers
They migrate upstream against the current

items.reveal:
Helical flow concentrates velocity on the outer bend (river cliff, undercut) and slows it on the inner bend (point bar, deposition). The thalweg (line of fastest flow) traces an S-curve.

Mississippi meander cutoffs were mapped by Harold Fisk for the US Army Corps of Engineers in 1944 — showing the river's channel migrating across tens of kilometres of floodplain over centuries. The Corps now actively manages cutoffs.

Oxbow lakes form when erosion narrows a meander neck until the river breaks through and abandons the loop.
items.why: Floodplains are dynamic. Property and infrastructure built across meandering rivers face migration as well as flooding hazards — a slower but inevitable risk.
